newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Blast death toll rises as Russia mourns dead.
newsitem.headline: Blast death toll rises as Russia mourns dead.

text.p: Flags flew at half mast in Russia on Tuesday, a day of mourning for at least 64 people killed in a weekend explosion at a military apartment block in the southern Dagestan region.
The emergencies ministry said eight bodies had been pulled from the wreckage on Monday night, raising the death toll to 64. Twenty children were among the dead.
A ministry spokeswoman said 103 people had been rescued since Saturday's explosion and eight, including four children, were still in hospital.
Two men were still unaccounted for. They had been guarding the nine-storey concrete building, housing mostly families of border guards, which collapsed like a pack of cards.
The building was not connected to the gas mains and officials suspect sabotage.

President Boris Yeltsin declared Tuesday a day of national mourning. He ordered flags to fly at half mast across the country and asked mass media not to broadcast light entertainment programmes as a mark of respect.
